artifacts.layout: Each run lives in runs/<scene>/<approach>/<run_id>/; tool files in d2s/, each stage's results in d2s/stages/<stage>/. Runs made on Kaggle land in the same place after pulling their results.
metrics.group.quality_hint: Rendered images compared with real camera images on the held-out test frames. Higher PSNR and SSIM, lower LPIPS are better. How it is measured: right after training (end of train.py) the model re-renders every test image (frames held out by the split, never trained on); renders are rounded to 8 bits like the source images, compared with the real camera image one by one and averaged; the eval.standard stage reads the result.
metrics.group.region_hint: PSNR over one image region only. People and vehicles cover few pixels, so whole-image PSNR hides their quality; they are the hardest part of a driving scene. How it is measured: right after training (end of train.py) the model re-renders every test image (frames held out by the split, never trained on); renders are rounded to 8 bits like the source images, compared with the real camera image one by one and averaged; the eval.standard stage reads the result.
metrics.group.time_hint: Real training time, total time from data preparation to scene.ply, and iterations trained.
metrics.group.resources_hint: Peak training VRAM, model render speed, and the GPU used. Only comparable between runs on the same GPU.
metrics.group.size_hint: A 3D scene is built from many Gaussians, each a small coloured blob in space. More Gaussians give more detail but heavier files and slower rendering. After training the model is saved in three forms for three jobs, hence three numbers: the full model (used for evaluation), the PLY file (static scene for other tools) and the preview package (viewed on the 3D viewer page, with cars moving over time).
compare.chart.pareto_hint: Each dot is a run. Runs ringed in yellow and joined by the dashed line are on the Pareto front: no other run has both higher PSNR and a better horizontal value. Runs below it have a better alternative on both counts.
compare.chart.regions_hint: Each group of bars is a run: whole image, people, vehicles, moving objects. Shows which approach reconstructs people and vehicles well, which whole-image PSNR hides.
compare.chart.breakdown_hint: Time per stage group from data preparation to scene.ply. Faded parts were reused from the cache (counted at the original run time).
compare.chart.curves_hint: Training curves of up to 6 runs, read from metrics.json. Shows which run converges faster, and whether a 3000-step quick test already shows the trend. This PSNR is measured on training images, so it is higher than test PSNR.
metrics.group.summary_hint: The main metric of each group below. Ranked by Avg (PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS combined) by default; click another column header to sort by it, every table follows.
metrics.hint.avg: Mip-NeRF's combined score: geometric mean of 10^(−PSNR/10), √(1 − SSIM) and LPIPS, three quantities expressed as errors. Lower is better. No weights, and a run's score does not change when other runs are added. Computed from the three metrics next to it, so measured at the same time.
metrics.hint.psnr: PSNR (dB, higher is better): per-pixel colour error between the rendered and the real camera image, −10·log10(MSE), over valid pixels. Sensitive to misalignment, lenient on blur. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.ssim: SSIM (0–1, higher is better): local structural similarity (luminance, contrast, edges), skimage structural_similarity over the whole image. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.lpips: LPIPS (lower is better): perceptual difference from AlexNet features (torchmetrics); closest to human judgement, catches blur that PSNR misses. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.human: PSNR over image regions with people only (cyclists and motorcyclists included): the rectangle around each projected 3D box, objects fully inside the frame. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.vehicle: PSNR over image regions with cars, buses and trucks only: the rectangle around each projected 3D box. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.dynamic: PSNR over all moving objects (people and vehicles) together. Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.occupied: PSNR over every region except the sky (sky mask from prep.masks_segformer). Measured once right after training, on every test image (frames not used for training).
metrics.hint.train_time: Real training time: training steps only (data, forward, backward, update), summed over resumes; excludes start-up, checkpoint loading, preview renders, checkpoint saving and final evaluation. Measured during training, saved with each checkpoint (train_stats.json).
metrics.hint.recon_time: Total time of the stages from data preparation until scene.ply is written, from the per-stage times the engine records in run.json; cached stages count their original run time. Computed when building the table.
metrics.hint.iters: Iterations (steps) trained, read from train_stats.json written with the last checkpoint.
metrics.hint.vram: Peak VRAM of the training process (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated), the maximum over resumes. Measured during training, not evaluation.
metrics.hint.fps: Frames the model renders per second, measured while evaluating the test set right after training, on the training GPU: model render time only (the approach's renderer, every part of the model), first frames skipped. Not the 3D viewer page speed.
metrics.hint.gpu: GPU of the machine that ran the run, recorded when the run starts or resumes (env.json); several GPUs means it resumed on another machine.
metrics.hint.gaussians: Gaussians in the trained model, covering everything it reconstructs: background, cars, people, deformable objects. This is the most complete number and the model used for PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS. Counted when the final checkpoint is saved.
metrics.hint.ply_gaussians: Gaussians in scene.ply, written automatically at the end of every run by the export.ply_world stage: a single file holding the static scene, for other 3DGS viewers or tools. It holds the static background of the whole stretch driven (all frames merged). By default there are no cars; setting rigid_frame of the export.ply_world stage adds the cars, frozen at that frame. People, deformable objects, the sky and almost transparent Gaussians are always dropped, so this is smaller than the model count. The preview package's .ply files are not included (they have their own column).
metrics.hint.ply_size: Size of scene.ply (one file, the static scene; see the scene.ply Gaussians column).
metrics.hint.preview_gaussians: Gaussians in the preview package (Export preview button), summed over all its .ply files: background.ply for the background and one file per car in actors/. The package is viewed on the 3D viewer page: the background stays still and each car is moved and rotated per frame (not 4DGS); no people, and almost transparent Gaussians are dropped. Empty if the run has not exported it.
metrics.hint.preview_size: Total size of the preview package files: background, cars, and the per-frame car positions.
compare.side.info: Pick two runs to watch their test-set videos side by side; Play starts both videos together at the same time.
compare.arrows: Arrows next to metric names follow the paper convention: ↑ higher is better, ↓ lower is better. The small icon at the end of a header shows the sorted column and direction.
compare.sort.click: Click to sort by this column; click again to reverse
compare.by_split.label: Split display
compare.mixed_split: This table mixes runs from several splits ({splits}): this metric is measured on the split's test frames, compare it only between runs on the same split (see the Split column, or choose Group by split).
compare.chart.mixed_split: This chart mixes runs from several splits ({splits}): PSNR is measured on each split's test frames and does not compare across splits. Choose Group by split to colour and connect the Pareto front per split.
compare.chart.mixed_gpu: This chart has runs on different GPUs ({gpus}): time, VRAM and FPS depend on hardware, compare them only between runs on the same GPU.

viewer.mode.hint: Preview package: the browser draws the background and cars, cars move per frame; free camera; no people or sky. Static scene: the browser draws scene.ply, background only. Video: plays the MP4 videos the train stage rendered along the original cameras; everything is there but the camera is fixed. GPU render: the machine running Studio draws from the checkpoint with the original renderer, complete with a free camera; needs an NVIDIA GPU and a PyTorch environment.

viewer.mode.video.sub: Videos rendered along the original cameras

compare.mixed_software: Runs in this table used different library versions ({versions}). A different PyTorch or gsplat version can shift metrics, time and Gaussian counts even with the same configuration, so small gaps between runs may come from versions rather than the approach. See each run's versions on its run page.
new.env.ok: The {env} environment on this machine has the expected versions
new.env.warn: The {env} environment on this machine has different versions: the run works, but results may differ from other runs
new.env.missing: This machine lacks the {env} environment: the run will fail at the train step
new.env.install_hint: Create the conda env from {file}, run this script inside it, then reopen Studio with that env's Python. It takes a while because gsplat-geer, nvdiffrast and pytorch3d are built. Kaggle notebooks install it themselves. The SMPL model file is not installed by the script: download it from smpl.is.tue.mpg.de (account and licence needed) and put it at <workdir>/smpl_models/SMPL_NEUTRAL.pkl, or point D2S_SMPL_MODEL at it.
scene.splits.range_hint: First and last frame of the split, inclusive (0 to {last}). Default: the whole scene. A short range makes trial runs faster.
